name: Rivern Frostwind
summary: At Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind trains riders and guards Winterspring's frostsabers. His frost tiger Glacier is at his side, and only the most dedicated Alliance champions earn the honor of riding one.

sections.title: Master of the Frostsabers
sections.body:
From icy Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind oversees the breeding and care of Winterspring frostsabers. Unlike the nightsabers of Teldrassil and Ashenvale, these cats are bred to endure northern Kalimdor's bitter cold.

Rivern entrusts a saber only to those who prove their commitment to protecting the beasts. They must gather fresh meat from the tundra, clear out Winterfall furbolgs, and drive back rampaging frost giants before he deems them worthy.

faq.answer: At Frostsaber Rock, Rivern Frostwind is a night elf riding master and caretaker of the Wintersaber Trainers faction. With his tiger Glacier, he protects and properly rears Winterspring's powerful native big cats.

Rivern lives at Frostsaber Rock to train riders and safeguard the region's rare white frostsabers. Aggressive Winterfall furbolgs, encroaching giants, and harsh conditions threaten the predators, so he keeps order and looks after their well-being.

faq.q: Can Horde players work with Rivern?
faq.answer: No. Rivern Frostwind is loyal to the night elves and the Alliance. He refuses to deal with Horde travelers at Frostsaber Rock and reserves his trust and mount training for Alliance champions.

faq.q: Who is the tiger beside him?
faq.answer: Glacier is the frost tiger beside Rivern. He is Rivern's personal companion and a fine example of the hardy cats native to the Winterspring tundra.

angles.text: For the Alliance, Rivern Frostwind is the sole provider of the rare Winterspring Frostsaber. Riders beyond Darnassus can earn the chance to tame one of Kalimdor's fiercest beasts through perseverance.

As a night elf, you know nightsabers are closely tied to Elune's priesthood and Kalimdor's sentinels. Rivern's frostsabers belong to an adapted, solitary lineage bred for Winterspring's harsh snowscapes.
